title: Attacking the tb=B escape: the regime is flatter, but not reachable by rule

smi: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, GPU-0c7c3a68-f18e-7947-fbdb-bdadaff4c4d7, 81559 MiB, 1980 MHz, 610.57.04, 4

schedule.note: 22 consecutive ODD batch sizes in ONE run, so width is 1 throughout and the tile ordering is consistent -- which also fixes the first-tile extraction confound of the earlier merged analysis

bands.reading: tb=B forms two clean contiguous bands, [59,63] and [121,127], not scattered points

the_upper_cut.finding: CLEAN and NECESSARY. tb=B forces ty=1 and tx=8, so the tile is 24B elements and must fit the budget (1536 or 3072).
the_upper_cut.verified: 2 of 2, and it is exactly where each band ends
the_upper_cut.but: NOT SUFFICIENT: B = 51..57 and 113..119 all fit the budget and still take a power of two

the_lower_cut.status: UNSOLVED. Every simple predictor overlaps between the two classes.

tested.verdict: separates 20 of 22 in THIS run, but REFUTED by eight counterexamples in earlier data: B = 45,47,75,77,79,91,93,95 all have B mod 16 in {11,13,15} and took a power of two
overlaps: 0.922 is tb=B but 0.930 is power of two

the_lower_cut.why_it_matters: the mod-16 rule was refuted using data already in hand, without spending a run -- the fifth post-hoc pattern to die in this work, and the first caught before measuring

the_practical_result.finding: THE tb=B REGIME IS MEASURABLY FLATTER, which is the standardisation goal even without a rule to reach it
the_practical_result.caveat: the bands sit at different B, so the a/B trend contributes to the MEANS; the flatness comparison is within-band and not affected by it

what_to_do: No closed-form rule reaches the tb=B regime, but the tile is visible at COMPILE TIME in about 40 seconds, so the bands can be FOUND by compiling candidates rather than predicted. That is the same procedure as the tile-signature selector, now with a sharper target: prefer a batch whose heavy-kernel tile has tb = B, because its neighbourhood is 2.4 to 3.5 times flatter.
limits: One run, one GPU, 3600 sweeps, 7 repeats, dispersion 0.2-0.5%.
Only two bands observed, both just below a power of two, so whether the pattern repeats below 256 is untested.
The flatness claim rests on 5 neighbour jumps inside tb=B bands against 11 outside; the direction is consistent but n is small.
Everything at Rd=18.30, L=5, N=39 on one XLA build.
